models.title: Marginal consumption response to additional disposable income
models.summary: Citation correction to prior r1: MPC is the share of an additional disposable-income unit that is spent; the remainder is MPS.

relationship.original_equation: MPC=delta consumption / delta disposable income; MPS=1-MPC
relationship.locator: Learning Module3, Relationship among Saving, Investment, the Fiscal Balance and the Trade Balance, printed p142 (PDF p154), unnumbered MPC prose and MPS complement
relationship.translation_notes: Both changes have currency dimensions, giving a fraction. MPS=1-MPC is the complementary allocation from the same partition and is retained here as a special solve/composition note. Nonzero income change is enforced as dY squared positive because the engine has no != operator. Revisionr2 replaces an insufficient or inaccessible corroboration locator with a directly inspected page containing the actual formula definition; equation and numeric cases unchanged.

variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: Source assumption: other consumption determinants are held fixed.
Source model: a conventional positive marginal allocation has0<=MPC<=1; this is an economic scope condition, not required by division alone.
limitations: A finite difference is a local marginal response only if the response is linear over that interval or interpreted in the infinitesimal limit.
Average propensity C/Y is distinct and is not a reliable general estimator of MPC.
